channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Sideways bias holds above support against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann maintain a constructive short-term view on USD/SGD, noting recent sideways trade around 1.2760.

item.title: Banxico expected to stay put as inflation risks block easing – Reuters
item.description: A Reuters poll shows that all economists expect that the Mexican Central Bank (Banxico) will hold rates unchanged at 6.50% for the third straight meeting on Thursday.

item.title: ECB’s Nagel says restrictive policy cannot be ruled out
item.description: The Bundesbank President and European Central Bank (ECB) member Joachim Nagel crossed the wires at a financial event in London on Tuesday, acknowledging that high energy prices had driven inflation off its 2026 target.

item.title: Mexican Peso carry cushion thins as USD/MXN breaks 100-day SMA
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) extended its losses for the third straight trading session on Tuesday, down over 0.4% as investors reduce their exposure to the Mexican currency following last week’s Federal Reserve (Fed) decision to raise interest rates.

item.title: South Korean Won: Export surge supports BoK stance – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank reports South Korea’s exports for the first 20 days of September jumped 78.3% year-on-year, extending nine months of double-digit growth and led by a 259% surge in semiconductor exports.

item.title: Taiwan Dollar: Equity inflows support TWD againt US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that the Taiwan Dollar (TWD) has extended gains, briefly strengthening near 31.71 versus the US Dollar (USD), supported by strong foreign portfolio inflows and domestic equity outperformance tied to tech and AI themes.

item.title: Gold losses altitude as peace hopes meet hawkish Fed bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price retreats from daily highs of $4,376 on Tuesday as US Treasury yields rise and the US Dollar continues to strengthen, with investors pricing in further Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening towards year-end. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades at $4,337, down 0.14%.

item.title: Asia FX: AI-driven support for regional currencies – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan notes that improved risk sentiment and AI optimism around Meta’s Muse supported a slightly stronger Dollar and stable DM yields.

item.title: Forex Today: Advanced PMIs in the limelight, but what about the UN General Assembly?
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) has extended its recovery on Tuesday, climbing to new multi-week highs on the back of steady bets for extra Fed tightening, while increasing hopes of a potential deal to unlock the US-Iran-Hormuz conflict seem to have been ignored by market participants.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Gradual decline within tight bands – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) strategists Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann expect USD/CNH to edge lower intraday but stay confined to a narrow 6.6890–6.6960 range, with a clear break below 6.6890 seen as unlikely. Over one to three weeks, they see downside extending toward 6.6820 as momentum builds.

item.title: WTI extends decline as Trump signals progress in talks with Iran
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil extends its decline on Tuesday as traders assess fresh Middle East developments, keeping energy prices under pressure for a fifth straight day. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $89.50, near a two-week low.

item.title: Trump signals diplomatic push on Ukraine and Iran as diesel ban looms
item.description: US President Donald Trump is figuring out a solution to end the war between Russia and Ukraine, after meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Furthermore, he added that Russian President Vladimir Putin is willing to meet to end the war.

item.title: South Korean Won: Export surge supports KRW recovery – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong report that the Korean Won (KRW) strengthened alongside gains in tech equities, lower Oil prices and strong export data, including a surge in semiconductor shipments.

item.title: US Dollar Index pushes higher on the case for another Fed increase
item.description: The Dollar Index trades near 100.70, its highest level since late July. It has climbed through five straight sessions of falling Crude Oil, the opposite of how the war has moved it for most of this year. The Fed is the reason.

item.title: Fed’s Barkin backs rate hike, stays unsure on more increases
item.description: Richmond Federal Reserve (Fed) President Thomas Barkin said on Tuesday that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided to raise interest rates last Wednesday because inflation risks outweighed those to maximum employment.

item.title: British Pound sinks as USD shrugs off Hormuz reopening hopes
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) dives over 0.17% against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday amid newswire reports that Tehran intends to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the United States meets certain conditions. At the time of writing, GBP/USD trades at 1.3343 after peaking at 1.3387.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average drops from a weekly high as bank shares slide
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) rose on Tuesday to its highest level since September 14 before the opening bell, then turned lower once trading started in New York. It trades near 51,800, below Monday's close. The NASDAQ Composite tested record highs and the S&P 500 is barely changed.

item.title: Canadian Dollar dips as Oil slump, dovish BoC outlook underpin USD
item.description: USD/CAD gains 0.27% on Tuesday and trades around 1.4070 at the time of writing, supported by weakness in the Canadian Dollar (CAD).

item.title: Gold consolidates as Iran diplomacy hopes clash with hawkish Fed expectations
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates on Tuesday as traders weigh fresh Middle East headlines while the broader geopolitical backdrop remains tense. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,328 after rebounding from an intraday low of $4,291 during European trading hours.

item.title: Oil: Headlines drive vulnerability – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay and Bart Melek highlight that elevated speculative positioning leaves Crude Oil vulnerable to shifting headlines around Middle East supply routes.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Recovery stalls below key moving averages
item.description: USD/JPY trades flat on Tuesday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) holds firm in thin holiday trading during Japan’s Silver Week. However, a broadly stronger US Dollar (USD) keeps the Yen’s gains in check. At the time of writing, USD/JPY trades around 157.46.

item.title: Trump sees post-election Iran deal, calls for pressure to stay
item.description: US President Donald Trump said at the UN General Assembly that “we must be united in maintaining pressure on Iran,” adding that he believes that the US and Iran will strike a deal following the US midterm elections in November.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Slack delays hikes despite crude shock – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada's Ethan Currie notes that while oil-driven inflation risks have increased, the Bank of Canada is likely to remain on hold in October as domestic slack and trade uncertainty continue to weigh on the economic outlook.

item.title: United States: September inflation profile – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Oscar Munoz and Eli Nir provide an early projection for United States (US) September Consumer Price Index (CPI , expecting Headline CPI to rise 0.54% m/m, driven mainly by an almost 8% jump in gasoline and firmer food prices.

item.title: Natural gas: Price downside limited – Commerzbank
item.description: Norman Liebke at Commerzbank argues that European gas prices may see only limited further declines despite a brief 8% drop on US–Iran diplomatic headlines.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: USD strength keeps CAD weakness in focus - Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is largely unchanged, with Governor Macklem’s comments leaving the Bank of Canada (BoC) outlook broadly consistent with the latest policy statement.

item.title: Fed’s Collins: More restrictive policy should help inflation return to 2%
item.description: Boston Federal Reserve (Fed) President Susan Collins said in a LinkedIn post on Tuesday that she supported last week’s interest-rate hike and sees a somewhat more restrictive policy stance as appropriate to bring inflation sustainably back to the Fed's 2% target.

item.title: Risk sentiment improved and Oil prices fell: Why the US Dollar is still holding firm
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) remains on a solid footing following a hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate decision and persistent hawkish rhetoric from Fed officials.

item.title: Euro remains cautious as Middle East headlines, Fed outlook drive sentiment
item.description: EUR/USD is little changed on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) gives back earlier gains following fresh diplomatic signals surrounding the war between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Silver edges lower as demand-led inflation keeps Fed tightening risks in focus
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) declines 0.38% on Tuesday and trades around $65.85 at the time of writing.
